business_problem: Kiabi sought to escape 70% uptime and failing legacy Oracle servers by modernizing its data core to support global scale and omnichannel retail.
solution_summary: Kiabi sought to escape 70% uptime and failing legacy Oracle servers by modernizing its data core to support global scale and omnichannel retail. Kiabi migrated to MongoDB Atlas on GCP, building a multi-region cluster to secure its sales repository and loyalty data with 100% resilience. Kiabi Kiabi leaves behind legacy limits for cloud leadership Kiabi sought to escape 70% uptime and failing legacy Oracle servers by modernizing its data core to support global scale and omnichannel retail. Our Solution Kiabi migrated to MongoDB Atlas on GCP, building a multi-region cluster to secure its sales repository and loyalty data with 100% resilience. Outcome Kiabi achieved 100ms response times and high availability, using 13 MongoDB Atlas clusters to scale through its most successful sales year ever.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational data and provides the managed document database foundation for Kiabi's workload.

data_flow: Customer documents, metadata, and related business records are stored in MongoDB Atlas and made available to search, audit, or user-facing workflows.

Their Challenge Kiabi sought to escape 70% uptime and failing legacy Oracle servers by modernizing its data core to support global scale and omnichannel retail.
Outcome Kiabi achieved 100ms response times and high availability, using 13 MongoDB Atlas clusters to scale through its most successful sales year ever.

With an uptime of around 70% in the previous environment, payments could be processed in-store without ever being successfully sent back to the central system, so staff had to painstakingly re-integrate all transactions.

“I can't imagine having to tell clients, ‘You’ve lost the 600 points you accumulated throughout the year — your discount has disappeared’.” To build internal momentum, Kiabi appointed ambassadors to champion the transition, and supported their advocacy with a quick-win project to demonstrate the platform's power: while their legacy setup required nearly a week for deployment and monitoring, the team proved they could achieve full self-sufficiency on Google Cloud and MongoDB in just two days.
